correctness.rationale: The four ranking types have plurality (a,b+c,d) and Borda (2a+b,n+b+c,c+2d). A unique Borda extreme winner forces the same plurality winner. A unique Borda middle winner opposite A-plurality is equivalent to a>max(b+c,d) and a<d+b+2c; reflection doubles the weighted multinomial cone. At t*=log(2)/2, tilting the a-b-c walk produces centered span-one increments with variance 2sqrt(2)/(1+2sqrt(2)); remaining inequalities have strict tilted slack. Their errors decay exponentially, and a lattice local limit plus bounded weighted summation supplies the explicit 1/sqrt(n) constant. Independent enumeration over all 4^n ballots for n=1..7 agrees, including 24/256 at n=4. Finite checks are not the asymptotic proof.
residual_risks: A large-n asymptotic requires the stated lattice local limit and strict tilted slack, not the finite enumeration.
